findings.title: The cumulative-budget controls are set by the loop's run count, not by what the loop needs: held-out tasks are charged runs x B although no decision reads them, and the control's value jumps with the number of rejected runs
findings.explanation:
PREDICTIONS_HYBRID.md l.21-22, l.27 (R3) and l.65 fix the control as the registered enumeration and the generation-0 machinery run once at runs x B on every task. Three things make that comparison unlike-for-like.
(1) loop.py:105 runs all eight partitions on every move 'for the record' (docstring l.12-13), but acceptance reads the learning partitions only (l.218). The loop's held-out count is therefore measured at B candidates per held-out task, while the control gives each held-out task runs x B. In my 4-run loop 67% of the cumulative candidates went to held-out tasks. What the loop needs (learning tasks every run, held-out once with the final state) is 2.21 x B per task, against the planned 4 x B; at 24 runs it is 10.25 x B in configuration A and 15.56 x B in configuration B, against 24 x B.
(2) The multiplier is report['runs'] (loop.py:243), which counts every rejected move and every run after the best state. In the tiny loop the best state was reached at run 3 of 4, and 2 of the 4 runs were rejected moves.
(3) The control is very sensitive to the multiplier. Tiny scale, generation-0 SCf held-out: 26 at 300, 39 at 663, 43 at 900, 46 at 1200, 51 at 2000. Real scale, from the registered records through hybrid.registered(): the registered control at runs x 10^4 is 32 held-out for 1-3 runs, 48-50 for 4-19 runs, 67 at 20 runs, 71 at 21 and 73 at 22-24 runs. Generation 0 of the hybrid (SCf at 10^4) is 61 in the experimenters' own log. So 'beats the registered enumeration at the cumulative budget' is true for any loop that stops by run 19 and false for one that reaches run 20, with nothing learned in either case.
The over-charge works in favour of the experimenters' own predictions H6 and H13 (R3 fails). In the other direction the control misses that the loop gets one verifier verdict per learning task per run and selects among states on them, where the control gets one. Equal ceilings are also not equal spend: the loop actually spent 323,219 candidates, the control at 1200 spent 292,222.
Caveat: in my tiny run the loop's best state (held-out 23) is below every control, including generation 0 at the same budget (26), so the verdict there does not depend on the choice. The finding is about the margin and about the binary R3 when loop gains are not small.

findings.title: The held-out total is a raw sum over six partitions of 12 to 100 tasks: its sign differs from the per-partition picture, and in configuration B it is FRESH-2 alone
findings.explanation:
loop.py:107-108 and hybrid.py:550 add solved counts across partitions. Sizes are validation 12, far 12, far2 21, fresh1 33, fresh2 100, compose24 24: FRESH-2 is 100 of the 202 held-out tasks in configuration A and 100 of 124 in configuration B. Every prediction about held-out (R1, H2, H3, H9, H12, H13) is stated on that sum.
In my tiny loop the accepted apoptosis step changes the sum from 26 to 23, which reads as 'apoptosis lowers held-out' (H9). Per partition, two rise (validation +2 of 12, far2 +3 of 21), two fall (far -1 of 12, fresh2 -7 of 100) and two are flat; the unweighted mean of the six partition rates rises by 2.6 points. The sign of the held-out effect depends on the aggregate.
In the experimenters' record at 10^4 (gen0_1e4_f.json) the gain of SCf over the registered engine is +29 held-out, of which +15 (52%) is FRESH-1, a 33-task partition on which the map-shift pilot was already known when the predictions were written (PREDICTIONS_HYBRID.md l.5-6); FRESH-2 contributes +5 of 100. H1's threshold of 10 is met by FRESH-1 alone. COMPOSE-24 is 0 of 24 in every 10^4 row of the logs, so configuration B's 'held-out composition solves' is the FRESH-2 count.
The tasks are also clustered: near has 100 tasks in 22 families, far2 21 in 5, compose24 24 in 4, fresh1 33 in 15 (family field of rsi5/results_p1). In the tiny loop the three far2 gains are two drop-k tasks and one take-k task.

findings.title: A loop that ends on the run cap books a rollback that never happened
findings.explanation: When max_runs is reached in the middle of the move sweep, loop.py:204-205 breaks out of the sweep with accepted still False. Control then falls into the rollback branch (l.231-241): rollbacks is incremented, the current accepted step is put on the ban list and the log says 'no move accepted after ...', although the remaining moves at that state were never tried. The while condition then ends the loop. report['runs'] is correct (it equals len(timeline) and the harness run count, rejected moves included); report['rollbacks'] and the log are one too high.
findings.repro: The stated tiny command with the unmodified harness, from cd T: PYTHONPATH=T:H python3 H/loop.py 300 SCf W/out.json A 2 --max-runs 4 --random-control
findings.observed: 'run 3 apoptosis@1 learn 59 ... accepted apoptosis: learn 51 -> 59, held-out 26 -> 23'; 'run 4 compress@3 learn 55 held-out 21'; then 'rollback 1: no move accepted after apoptosis@run3; banned it and returned to run 1'; final line 'runs 4, rollbacks 1'. The timeline holds one move tried at state 3 (compress@3); apoptosis, unused and entropy were never run there. report['runs'] = 4 = len(timeline); the random-control run is a fifth harness run and is, correctly, not in report['runs'].
findings.effect_on_results: Any loop that stops on the 24-run cap reports one rollback more than it made, at zero runs of cost. H4 (a rollback costs at least 3 extra runs and changes the best learning count by at most 1) would be judged on a count that includes it. The best state and the run count are unaffected.
findings.fix: After the sweep, if harness.runs >= max_runs, record the stop reason (for example report['stopped_by'] = 'max_runs') and break before the rollback branch.

findings.title: A fused solve is booked one candidate after the engine has used its whole share: with switch F the direct route ends at budget + 1, and to_solution is not the budget a task needs
findings.explanation:
_search gives the engine its whole share (l.385) and then adds one per fused triple (l.393), up to three. On the direct route with switch F the share is the whole remainder (l.460), so a fused solve lands at budget + 1 (at most budget + 3). With switch f the extra candidate is spent in the sub-problem and taken off the direct remainder, so there is no overshoot; with E the reserve absorbs it.
The same booking makes to_solution a property of the run, not of the task. A fused solve is always at share + 1 whatever pool it needed: all 24 map+fused solves in gen0_1e4_f.json have to_solution 5001. A direct solve after a failed shift includes the sub-problem's spend, which is half of whatever budget was given. So the rule hybrid.registered() applies to the registered engine (solved and candidates_to_solution <= b) does not carry over to hybrid records.

findings.effect_on_results: Claim (2) is literally false for the F rows (SF and SCF at 10^4 with 11 'fused' solves each, SCF at 10^5 with 10): those solves were returned at candidate budget + 1. The size is one candidate in 10^4, so no count changes for that reason, and the loop's configuration (f) is not affected. The to_solution point matters only if a solve-at-budget curve or a cumulative-budget control for the hybrid is read off a larger run instead of being run: at tiny scale that reading is wrong in both directions.

findings.title: hybrid.registered() returns the 10^6 count for any larger budget without saying so
findings.explanation: registered() counts records with candidates_to_solution <= budget from a registered run whose own budget is 10^6 (rsi5/runs/p1.json). Above 10^6 nothing was measured, and the function returns the 10^6 count unchanged. rsi5/phase1.py load_plan refuses a report budget above the run budget for exactly this reason; registered() has no such check. 153 of the 338 registered searches were cut off at 10^6 with no match, so their outcome above that is unknown.

coverage:
Paths: T = <scratch>/tree, H = <scratch>/harness_snapshot, W = <scratch>/review_work/find-budget-fairness. Nothing under T or H was modified.

METHOD. W/instr holds byte-identical copies of loop.py and compress.py and a copy of hybrid.py patched by W/patch_hybrid.py to record, per task, every Engine.search call (share, reserve, engine budget, candidates, seconds, points), every fusion pass (pool sizes, value comparisons, mask tests, seconds), every mutation pass, and the time of shift detection, constant abduction, lifted re-checks and install. W/check_identical.py found 0 differences in 1014 records against the unmodified harness, and the instrumented loop's timeline equals the unmodified loop's. Runs: variants -, S, Sf, SCf, SCF, SCfE at 300; SCf, SCF, SCfE at 2000; SCf at 663, 900, 1200; '-' at 2000; the loop at 300 SCf A, 4 runs (with and without --random-control). All 338 tasks each time, 2 workers. Wall-clock ratios come from a busy machine and are rough; candidate and operation counts are exact.

DID NOT BREAK.
- Per-task spend. In every task of every run the record field 'candidates' equals the real spend (engine + fused + mutated). With f, with E, with learned abstractions and with keep cuts (the loop's runs) no task exceeded the budget. The only overshoot is +1 on direct fused solves with F (finding 4). The experimenters' 10^4 record also has max candidates 10000.
- Budget split. The shifted sub-problem share was budget // 2 in every shifted task, the direct route got budget minus spent, and the engine never exceeded its share (share minus reserve). With E the reserve was share // 10.
- Comparison (a). The harness with every component off equals the registered records task by task at 300 and at 2000 (338 tasks, 0 mismatches in solved, program, to_solution against candidates_to_solution, and candidates). The 10^4 log agrees per partition (89).
- Budget monotonicity of solved sets. SCf lost no task from 300 to 1200 to 2000.
- Loop run accounting. report['runs'] = len(timeline) = harness runs and includes rejected moves; a rollback costs no run; the --random-control run is outside the loop and is not counted.
- Entropy. A mutant costs 51-72 microseconds, 0.5-0.9 of an engine candidate, and is counted one each. 76-84% of the withheld reserve is never spent (unsolved tasks end at about 92% of the budget), which is a handicap for E, not an advantage. E lost 0 tasks at 300 and at 2000 (gained 3 at 2000), and in the 10^4 record no learning solve lies in the band a 10% reserve would cut.
- The spec shift buys no hidden compute: an element sub-problem candidate costs 24-41 microseconds against 57-79 for a whole-task candidate (median 19 against 25 evaluation points).

UNCOUNTED WORK, MEASURED (none of it large enough to explain a result).
- Fusion pass: 0.05-0.07% of engine wall time with f, 0.3-0.6% with F. One pass costs a median of 1 engine-candidate equivalent at 300 and 11 at 2000 (largest single value 272, on a loaded machine), against at most 3 counted. Operations per pass at 300 and at 2000: median 812 and 2761 value comparisons, median 32 and 469 mask tests, maximum 530 and 5724 mask tests. Worst case at FUSE_CAP (3000 x 3000, W/fuse_scaling.py): 0.31 s for 9 million mask tests, roughly 5,000-10,000 candidate equivalents, reachable only with 3000 mask-distinct partial programs and 3000 predicates. What the budget unit does not show: one pass decides the public behaviour of up to 387,000 if-programs (3.6 million over the SCf run at 2000, for 33 counted candidates) and returns terms of size 5-13 where the engine had completed size 2-3. That is a different algorithm, cheap in time, not hidden compute.
- Near-miss scan plus mutants: 0.9-2.0% of engine time. Lifted re-check: 0.03-0.10 s per run. Constant abduction: under 0.012 s per run. Shift detection: 0.003 s per run. Constant table: 1 ms per worker per run. Second Engine construction for a shifted task: 5.4 ms, about 75 candidate equivalents (the engine's own set-up is uncounted in the registered runs too).
- Driver: compress.propose 0.055 s per call, symbols_of 0.023 s for 312 calls, together 0.7% of the 4-run loop's wall time.

NOT EXAMINED. Anything above budget 2000 (the 10^4 and 10^5 statements rest on the experimenters' logs and on gen0_1e4_f.json, and the fusion cost at those budgets is an extrapolation), a configuration B loop, more than 4 loop runs, and the information-flow, correctness and determinism claims except where they touched accounting. One observation outside my lens: constant_table has no witness for -53, and _install indexes the table without the guard that _with_constants has, so a learned nullary constant equal to -53 would raise KeyError in a worker.

findings.title: The verifier's one-query limit is per run, not per loop generation; rejected public matches are re-queried by later moves and decided at least one acceptance in the recorded B loop
findings.explanation: Harness.run passes generation=self.runs (hybrid.py:489-500), the harness's own run counter, so FrozenVerifier's limit can never fire. Every move trial is a new 'generation', and every task's hidden examples are queried once per run: 24 times in the recorded A loop, 23 in B, plus the random control. Within a run a rejected public match is handled as claimed: not retried (solve returns the first match and the task is blocked for that run), not counted, not put in the corpus or usage counts (loop.py:113-114). But the next move changes the vocabulary, the search returns a different public match, and that is submitted to the same hidden examples; if it passes it counts in new.learn > current.learn (loop.py:218). Acceptance is therefore an adaptive multi-query process against the learning tasks' hidden examples. On boolean tasks it lets wrong programs through, and they then enter state.programs (the compression corpus) and the usage counts that drive the cuts.

findings.title: One held-out task in configuration A is the same task as a learning task (identical public and hidden examples), and more are same-function twins
findings.explanation: CONFIGS takes the partitions as given. near/'caesar-cipher-k-modulo-n with k=4 and n=3' (learning in A) and validation/'caesar-cipher-k-modulo-n with k=1 and n=3' (held-out in A) have identical public example sets and identical hidden example sets: (x+4) mod 3 = (x+1) mod 3 on the same inputs. Programs of size k+1 are built from parts whose sizes sum to k, so one empty level does not mean later levels are empty. With the full vocabulary this never fires before the budget. loop.cut (lines 155-168) keeps the most used symbols, and hybrid._restrict (hybrid.py:315-323) hands that set to the engine (hybrid.py:382-385). In the element space the most used symbols are binary arithmetic and comparison primitives plus constants. If nothing kept builds a size-2 program (element space: neg, abs, range, is_prime, is_square; list space: head, tail, is_empty, length, or range with a kept constant), level 2 is empty and the engine stops after the variables and constants, although `add x 3` (size 3) is in the kept language. verdicts.title: A cut that leaves a space with no size-2 program stops the engine at size 2; the second apoptosis on the loop's own trajectory is such a cut
verdicts.evidence:
Reproduced with my own scripts in <scratch>/review_work/verify-semantics (drive.py, flip.py, show.py, exhaust_demo.py, usage_1e4.py). drive.py runs the unmodified loop.run_loop and only records each engine search's ending; with REVIEW_NO_STOP=1 it disables the stop at tree/rsi5/engine/bottomup.py:673-675 by marking the top context non-empty after ensure(), nothing else.

Code: the search ends 'exhausted' at the first size level where no context admits a program. A keep set with only binary primitives and constants has no size-2 program, so level 2 is empty although `add x 3` (size 3) is in the language. hybrid.py does not record `exhausted`.

One task (exhaust_demo.py, unmodified hybrid.solve): keep [add, int:-1, int:3, int:4, int:5, mod, sub], task xs -> x+3: unsolved after 14 of 300 candidates, both searches (exhausted, size 2, 7 candidates). Same keep plus `neg`: map (lambda x. add x 3) at candidate 15.

Loop, budget 300, moves apoptosis, 3 runs: run 2 apoptosis@1 59/23 accepted, 0 early stops. Run 3 apoptosis@2, element keep [add, eq, int:2, int:3, int:4, mod, sub]: learn 32 held-out 15; 79 of 86 element searches end exhausted at size 2 after 6 to 10 candidates (the other 7 match at size 1); lift-route solves 41 -> 6. Stop disabled, same spec: 57/30, no early stop.

Second cut at other budgets (flip.py, recorded -> stop disabled): 200: 32/15 -> 57/35; 400: 32/15 -> 54/29; 500: 32/15 -> 56/30; 2000 (element keep [add, int:-1, int:3, int:4, int:5, mod, sub]): 42/10 -> 61/20. Each has 79 dead element searches. Budget 1000 is not affected (keep holds range and is_empty; 71/38).

Decision flip, which the finder did not see: at budget 200 the parent has learn 53, so the second apoptosis is rejected as recorded (32) and accepted when measured (57). Full default loop at budget 200 run to its natural end: as is 10 runs, 2 rollbacks, best state run 6, learn 56, held-out 23. Stop disabled: 15 runs, 3 rollbacks, best state run 5, learn 57, held-out 35; the branch apoptosis -> unused -> apoptosis is accepted twice with held-out 19 -> 23 -> 29 (as is, that last step is recorded 32/9 and rejected).

Real budget: with loop's rule on the recorded 10^4 rows the first element cut keeps `range` (usage 6) as its only size-2 producer; the 7th rank is add / int:-1 at usage 7, so the second cut drops it unless usage shifts by one.

Not by-design-and-disclosed: tree/rsi5/ARCHITECTURE.md line 68 says the stop 'is not a proof that larger sizes add none; no record of the registered run has the flag set', which is about the registered full-vocabulary run. hybrid.py, loop.py and PREDICTIONS_HYBRID.md say nothing and the harness drops the flag.
verdicts.effect_on_results:
Every timeline row of a state whose keep set has no size-2 producer in a space (element space: neg, abs, range, is_prime, is_square; list space: head, tail, is_empty, length, range) records an engine stop, not a search of the kept language. Learn and held-out of those rows are too low by a wide margin: learn 32 instead of 54 to 57 at budgets 200 to 500, 42 instead of 61 at 2000; held-out 15 instead of 29 to 35, 10 instead of 20. At budgets 200 and 300 the recorded held-out change has the wrong sign (19 -> 15 recorded against 19 -> 35; 23 -> 15 against 23 -> 30).

The bias is toward rejecting every cut after the first, which is the predicted verdict V2 (saturation). It can change the headline: at budget 200 the loop's best state moves from learn 56 / held-out 23 to learn 57 / held-out 35, runs from 10 to 15, rollbacks from 2 to 3, and a branch with held-out rising in two consecutive accepted steps (the pattern R1 asks for) is hidden. At budgets 300, 400, 500 and 2000 the second cut is rejected either way (57 < 59, 54 < 65, 56 < 65, 61 < 80).

Whether it fires at 10^4 depends on one unit of usage; I could not run that budget. Not affected in my runs: generation 0, the first apoptosis, the unused cut, and the fixed-seed random control (its keep holds is_prime and range in the element space, range in the list space).
verdicts.fix: In hybrid.py record exhausted, completed_size and candidates of every engine search in the task row, and make the enumeration continue past an empty level with a harness-side wrapper (after bu.Context.ensure, keep the top context's added_at_level non-zero so the search ends only at max_size or at the budget; four lines, engine file untouched). Treat any row with 'exhausted, completed_size < MAX_SIZE, candidates < budget' as an invalid measurement, and re-measure every cut state.

verdicts.title: abstraction_use_learn and abstraction_use_held_out are counted by different rules, and the held-out one counts programs found without the symbol
verdicts.evidence:
Code (loop.py 117-127): a learning program goes through split_spaces first, so for a map+/filter+ route only the inner int lambda is folded; a held-out program is folded whole. A symbol whose body is the lift itself (lambda k xs. map (lambda x. ... k) xs) has list type and cannot match inside an int lambda.

Reproduced with the unmodified loop (loop.py 300 SCf out_a.json A 2 --max-runs 4) and my script use_rules.py in <scratch>/review_work/verify-semantics, which applies both rules to the same programs.

run 2 compress@1 (s1_1, s1_2, s1_3, all lift-shaped): every solved (program, route) is identical to generation 0, which had no symbol. Recorded use: learn {0, 0, 0}, held-out {s1_3: 1}. The held-out rule on the 51 learning programs gives {s1_1: 5, s1_2: 4, s1_3: 4}; the learning rule on the held-out programs gives 0. The one counted held-out program (fresh2 modulo-k, route map+search) is the same program as in generation 0.

run 4 compress@3 (s3_1, s3_2): recorded learn {0, 0}, held-out {s3_1: 3, s3_2: 1}. The held-out rule on the learning programs gives {s3_1: 3, s3_2: 2}; the learning rule on the held-out programs gives {s3_1: 1}. Three of the four counted held-out programs are lift-route programs identical to the previous state's; only compose24 trim-and-increment (route search, tail (map (lambda x. add x 1) xs)) is new in that run.

Both counters count occurrences per program, not solutions. Nothing in loop.py's docstring or PREDICTIONS_HYBRID.md states how use is counted.
verdicts.effect_on_results: abstraction_use_held_out is inflated: it counts S-lifted programs that the search built without the symbol (3 recorded against 1 real use in my run 4, 1 against 0 in run 2). H14 ('used in at most 2 verified held-out solutions') reads this field and would move toward FAIL, and any statement that a symbol transferred to held-out tasks, or that held-out use exceeds learning use, reads two numbers that are not comparable. abstraction_use_learn is 0 by construction for lift-shaped symbols on lift-route programs. No solved count and no accept/reject decision changes: the counters are not read by the loop, and the cuts use the learning rule on both spaces consistently.
verdicts.fix: Use one rule for both sides and count what the search built: have the worker return the admitted names that occur in the returned program's Expr tree before inlining, and count tasks, not occurrences. The smallest stopgap is to apply split_spaces in the held-out branch as well.

verdicts.title: A learned constant is counted under its abstraction name but cut under int:<value>: every cut removes it, and two learned constants of one value crash the run
verdicts.evidence:
Mechanism reproduced with my own stub (stub_const.py in <scratch>/review_work/verify-semantics): the unmodified loop.run_loop driven by scripted verified rows, its specs then given to the unmodified hybrid._install.

Scenario 1: 'propose s1_1: ((add 2) 5) score 5 tasks 4', accepted; abstraction_use_learn {s1_1: 5}. Spec of unused@2: constants [7], keep elem [gt, mul], keep list [cons, index, tail]; after _install both spaces have integer constants (). Spec of apoptosis@2: 18 symbols per space, without int:7, add, int:2 or int:5.

Scenario 2: 'propose s1_1: ((add 1) 5)' and 'propose s1_2: ((mul 2) 3)' in one step; spec constants [6, 6]; hybrid._install raises ValueError: duplicate integer constants.

Also: hybrid.constant_table has no entry for -53, and _install indexes the table without a check (hybrid.py 347).

Is the precondition reachable? nullary_scan.py on the recorded 10^4 SCf programs. Configuration A (train + near): no closed int subterm in any of the 80 learning programs and no nullary proposal in 8 proposal rounds. Configuration B: ((mul 2) 5) occurs in 5 learning tasks and ((add -1) -1) in 4; with the loop's ban rule compress proposes 'NULLARY ((mul 2) 5) score 7 tasks 5' in round 4 and ((add -1) -1) in round 8. No value has two printed forms in the recorded programs, so the crash is not triggered by them.
verdicts.effect_on_results: Conditional on an accepted compress step that admits a constant, which I did not observe (no compress step was accepted in any of my runs). If it happens, the next 'unused' and 'apoptosis' rows are measured without the learned constant, and in the apoptosis case without the pieces to rebuild it, so those rows lose solves and the cut is more likely to be rejected. Two learned constants of one value, or a learned -53, abort the run inside the workers. Configuration A cannot reach it from the recorded generation-0 programs; configuration B can.
verdicts.fix: Name a learned constant the same way everywhere: in symbols_of map a nullary abstraction's name to int:<value>. De-duplicate the values in serialise and skip values that have no entry in constant_table.

verdicts.title: The vector of an admitted abstraction is strict in arguments the inlined term never evaluates: a program that reproduces every public example is dropped
verdicts.evidence:
Code: _vector_of wraps the witness in bu._guarded, which returns ERR as soon as any argument value is ERR (bottomup.py 100-102); the engine's native map runs the lambda body only per element, and the reference interpreter is lazy.

Reproduced with strict_demo.py and strict_demo_lazy.py in <scratch>/review_work/verify-semantics (unmodified hybrid.solve, public examples only). Abstraction s = lambda k xs. map (lambda x. add x k) xs; crafted task xs -> each element plus head xs, with [] among the public inputs.

Keep [s, head, tail]: 'route None candidates 300 program None'. The pool holds the size-4 program; its inlined term map (lambda x. add x (head xs)) xs reproduces every public example in the reference interpreter, but its engine vector on the public inputs is [[6, 4, 7], ERR, [4, 9], [10]] against expected [[6, 4, 7], [], [4, 9], [10]]. Control keep [map, add, head, tail]: the same term at candidate 82. With my lazy vector (a failed argument passed on as a value that fails on use): found at candidate 8.

On the real tasks (lazy_vec.py: unmodified loop, moves compress and apoptosis, budget 300, 4 runs, two compress states with 3 and 2 symbols): the digest of counts, solved sets, programs and routes of every row is identical with the strict and the lazy vector. 14 of 36 train tasks and 52 of 100 near tasks have an empty-list public input, so the trigger exists in the data.

A wrong solve cannot result: every match is re-checked by the reference interpreter before it is returned.
verdicts.effect_on_results: It can only lower the solved count of a state that has learned symbols, so it biases against compress moves, toward the predicted verdict. No effect measured on the real tasks: all four rows identical at budget 300. No solved count is known to move.
verdicts.fix: Evaluate an admitted abstraction the way its inlined term is evaluated: pass a failed argument into the witness closure as a value that fails when used, and return ERR only if the result is or contains it.

verdicts.title: Reaching --max-runs in the middle of a state's moves is recorded as a rollback and bans the accepted move
verdicts.evidence:
Code: the move loop breaks at the cap (loop.py 204-205) with accepted still False; control falls into lines 231-241, which increment rollbacks, ban the current state's move and log 'no move accepted'.

Reproduced with the unmodified loop: loop.py 300 SCf out_a.json A 2 --max-runs 4. run 3 apoptosis@1 is accepted (learn 51 -> 59); run 4 compress@3 is rejected (55); then 'rollback 1: no move accepted after apoptosis@run3; banned it and returned to run 1' and 'runs 4, rollbacks 1'. Apoptosis, unused and entropy were never tried at the state of run 3.

It does not happen when the cap is reached right after an accepted move (max-runs 3: no rollback logged), or when the loop ends on its own: the default-cap run at budget 200 stopped at run 10 of 24 with 'no move accepted: stop'.
verdicts.effect_on_results: report['rollbacks'] and the final summary line are one too high, and the log reports a branch as dead that was not explored, whenever the run ends at the cap after a rejected move with moves still untried. H4's rollback accounting reads this number. The best state, every solved count and every earlier decision are unaffected, and the ban has no later effect because the loop ends.
verdicts.fix: Leave the while loop when the cap is reached inside the move loop, before the rollback branch (a flag set at the break and tested before line 231).

verdicts.title: Apoptosis keeps symbols by spelling when usage ties: 7 of the 17 kept list symbols at generation 0
verdicts.evidence:
Code: ranked = sorted(current, key=(usage, name)) and the first 60% are cut, so among symbols of equal usage the alphabetically last survive. PREDICTIONS_HYBRID.md and the loop.py docstring say only 'least used first'.

Reproduced with tiebreak.py in <scratch>/review_work/verify-semantics: generation 0, then the 60% cut computed with loop's rule under five orders among ties, each run once.

Budget 300, generation 0 learn 51 held-out 26; 17 of 42 element symbols used, 10 of 42 list symbols used, so 7 of the 17 kept list symbols are chosen by name alone (or, pair, range, snd, sub, unfold, zip). Results as learn / held-out: loop's order 59 / 23; name descending 58 / 22; three shuffles 58 / 27, 63 / 25, 63 / 24.

Budget 1000, generation 0 62 / 43, 6 list symbols chosen by name: learn 74 in all five orders; held-out 48 (loop's order), 49, 54, 50, 49.

Also visible in the unmodified loop at budget 300: apoptosis@1 (59 / 23) and unused@1 (58 / 24) differ only by those 7 name-chosen list symbols.

At 10^4, by loop's rule on the recorded SCf rows, 5 of the 17 kept list symbols (range, snd, sub, unfold, zip) and 2 of the 17 kept element symbols (unfold, zip) would be chosen by name.
verdicts.effect_on_results: The numbers reported for the accepted apoptosis carry an arbitrary component of several tasks. At budget 300 the learning gain is +7 to +12 depending on the order and the held-out change runs from -4 to +1, so H9 (an accepted apoptosis lowers held-out solves) passes with the loop's order and fails with one shuffled order. At budget 1000 the held-out count after the cut spans 48 to 54 and the loop's alphabetical order gives the lowest value. Held-out comparisons that start from the post-cut state (H9, and the best-state side of H13) inherit this spread. The accept decision did not flip in any of my ten runs, and the finder's reported held-out range of 22 to 23 is narrower than what I measured.
verdicts.fix: State the tie-break in the documentation and remove the arbitrary choice: when more than 60% of a space's symbols are unused, cut exactly the unused ones; otherwise break ties with a seeded shuffle and report the apoptosis row over several seeds.
